title: INTF-CLI socket log-compact verb reply: what the compaction (or its dry run) did or would do. Also the shape `pg-router log compact --json` prints, whether it ran against the daemon or offline.

dryRun.description: True when nothing was changed: the numbers are what a real run would do.

compacted.description: True when a real run rewrote the log. False for a dry run, and for a real run that found no progress possible (the log is already live state only) and so rewrote nothing.

noProgress.description: True when a compaction would not make the log smaller (bytesAfter >= bytesBefore).

via.description: Where it ran: inside the running daemon (over its socket), or offline against the log file with no daemon running.

eventsKept.description: Events still live (retained) that the compacted log keeps.

eventsDropped.description: Events whose final state is evicted: their records are discarded.

torn.description: True when the log has an undecodable line; everything from it on is ignored by a replay and discarded by a compaction.

durationMs.description: How long a real run took.

limitBytes.description: max_log_bytes, the denominator of the two percentages.

wouldRefuse.description: Dry run only: why a real run right now would be refused (the log is locked by another process).
